questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How the Japanese language has changed since 1999
Whether emojis help or harm the way we communicate
How to write emails that are clear and polite at work
Why online dating sites are becoming more popular
questions.why: They discuss emojis, the critics who dislike them, and an expert who says they make us better communicators.

questions.q: Why does Sam say hello to Neil in an unusual way at the start?
options: Because she has lost her voice and can't speak
Because Neil asked her to try something new
To show Neil how to use a new mobile phone
To introduce the topic by using emojis
questions.why: Sam greets Neil with a smiley face, high five and fist bump, then says they're entering the world of emojis.

questions.q: What are Sam's and Neil's favourite emojis?
options: Sam: tears of laughter; Neil: hearts
Sam: thumbs up; Neil: crying with laughter
Sam: smiling with hearts; Neil: high five
They both like the sad face emoji the most
questions.why: Sam's favourite is 'crying tears of laughter' and Neil likes 'smiling face with hearts'.

questions.q: According to Neil, why have emojis become so popular?
options: They are quicker to type than whole words
They were free on the first mobile phones
They add missing emotion to writing
They help people who can't read or write
questions.why: He says they let people put back some of the human emotion missing in written texts and emails.

questions.q: What do people who are not emoji fans believe?
options: Emojis are too difficult for older people to understand
Emojis make it harder to put feelings into words
Emojis should only be used by teenagers
Emojis are more useful in emails than in texts
questions.why: Neil says some believe carefully chosen words are best and emojis affect our ability to put feelings into words.

questions.q: What is Professor Vyv Evans's opinion of the critics of emojis?
options: They are right that we should return to Shakespeare
They are right, but emojis are too popular to stop
They understand communication better than most people
They misunderstand how communication really works
questions.why: He says their view 'fundamentally misunderstands the nature of communication'.

questions.q: What figures are given about emoji use?
options: Over 6 billion a day, most showing emotion
About 70 emoji messages a day sent by the average person
Over 3,000 new emojis are invented every single year
Only 6 percent of messages contain an emoji at all
questions.why: Sam says over 6 billion emoji messages are sent daily, about 70 percent with emotion-based characters.

questions.q: What did research by the dating site Match.com find?
options: People dislike partners who send too many emojis
Emojis often cause arguments between couples
People using more emojis get more dates
Most people stop using emojis once they are dating
questions.why: Vyv Evans says people who use more emojis 'tend to be lucky in love'.
